bib.title: StereoSet: Measuring stereotypical bias in pretrained language models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 59th Annual Meeting of the ACL and the 11th IJCNLP

read.skipped: target-term list tables in appendix skimmed

question: How strongly do pretrained language models exhibit stereotypical bias on natural text, measured together with their language-modeling ability?
hypothesis: Pretrained LMs trained on real-world data capture stereotypical biases; a bias measure must be paired with language-modeling ability to avoid misleading trust.
contributions: StereoSet, a large-scale natural English dataset of 16,995 CATs across gender, profession, race, religion
Intrasentence and intersentence Context Association Tests
Evaluation of BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet, GPT2 showing strong stereotypical bias that correlates with language-modeling ability

method.summary: Builds StereoSet, a crowdsourced benchmark of 16,995 Context Association Test triplets (stereotype, anti-stereotype, meaningless) in intrasentence and intersentence form over gender, profession, race, religion. Evaluates BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet, GPT2 (several sizes) and an ensemble with lms, ss and icat; the only training is a Next Sentence Prediction head for intersentence scoring.
method.task: measuring stereotypical bias and language-modelling ability of pretrained LMs by ranking associations

datasets.name: StereoSet
datasets.size: 16,995 triplets (8,498 intrasentence, 8,497 intersentence); 321 target terms; 4 domains
datasets.split: 25% of target terms (and instances) dev, 75% test, disjoint terms; no train set
datasets.source: Amazon Mechanical Turk, US workers, HIT acceptance >97%, $15/h; each example written by 1 worker, validated by 4 others; 475 intrasentence and 803 intersentence annotators; target terms from Wikidata (P106, P172, P140) and Nosek et al. 2002 for gender
datasets.preprocessing: kept CATs where >=3 of 5 validators agree (83% retained); manual filter of infrequent/fine-grained terms

datasets.name: Wikipedia NSP corpus
datasets.size: 9.5 million training examples; test set 3.5 million examples
datasets.source: built from Wikipedia: sentence i, sentence i+1, random negative from another article

datasets.name: Large Movie Review dataset (Maas et al. 2011)
datasets.preprocessing: used to fine-tune BERT sentiment classifier for dataset analysis and SentimentLM

models.name: ENSEMBLE
models.architecture: linear weighted combination of BERT-large, GPT2-medium, GPT2-large

training.objective: NSP head: binary classification, cross entropy (is sentence B the continuation of A); sentiment: movie review classification
training.optimizer: BertAdam for NSP head (BERT); Adam for sentiment classifier
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup from 50 steps to 500 steps (NSP, BERT)
training.batch_size: 80 sequences (20,480 tokens) for NSP; 32 for sentiment
training.epochs: 10 epochs over the NSP corpus; 7 epochs for sentiment
training.hardware: 2x RTX 2080 Ti for NSP heads; 2x Tesla V100 32GB for GPT2-large
training.compute: each model bias evaluation within 5 minutes

other.gpt2_nsp: mean-pooled representations over sequence fed to classification head
other.nsp_accuracy: RoBERTa-base 94.6, RoBERTa-large 97.1, XLNet-base 93.4, XLNet-large 94.1, GPT2 92.5, GPT2-medium 94.2, GPT2-large 96.1; 93-98% overall
other.note: other models use same details as BERT; 'until convergence' and 10 epochs both stated

inference.decoding: scoring only: rank candidate associations by likelihood
inference.samples: single evaluation per model; no seeds or runs stated

parameters.intrasentence_MLM_ll: log prob of attribute term filling the blank; multi-subword terms unmasked left to right, average per-subword probability
parameters.intersentence_ll: log likelihood from trained NSP head that attribute sentence follows context
parameters.pseudo_likelihood_intrasentence: attribute never masked; mask each context term one at a time
parameters.pseudo_likelihood_intersentence: pseudo-likelihood of context sentence conditioned on attribute sentence
parameters.gpt2_intrasentence: probability of the full sentence with blank instantiated
parameters.gpt2_pll_intersentence: ratio of joint probability of attribute sentence with and without the context

metrics.name: lms (language modeling score)
metrics.definition: percentage of instances where the model prefers the meaningful over the meaningless association; averaged over target terms

metrics.name: ss (stereotype score)
metrics.definition: percentage of examples where the model prefers stereotypical over anti-stereotypical association; averaged over target terms; ideal 50

eval.protocol: Dev/test split by target term; results on test set; no seeds, no confidence intervals or significance tests for ss/lms; Spearman correlation between lms and ss across models.

limits: Authors concede ideal StereoSet performance does not guarantee an unbiased model since bias manifests in many ways
Pretraining corpus size could not be tested by training the same model on more data (lack of compute)
icat assumes equal importance of lms and ss and is not intended as sole selection criterion
Dataset is US English and US stereotypes only; workers US-based
lms is not a full language-modeling evaluation
No variance across runs or seeds reported

terms.definition: an over-generalized belief about a particular group of people
a test that measures the language modeling ability as well as the stereotypical bias of pretrained language models
lms * min(ss, 100-ss)/50; ideal model 100, stereotyped model 0
